frequency_question: How often do announced major tariff threats with multi-month countdowns proceed to implementation without being delayed or replaced by an agreement?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly announced, high-salience US tariff rate hikes or broad import restrictions featuring a definitive future effective date published at least 60 days in advance. Excludes routine antidumping/countervailing duty administrative determinations.

cases.name: Section 232 Steel/Aluminum Tariffs (Initial Announcement to Implementation)
Section 301 China Tariffs (Tranche 1 Announcement to Implementation)
Proposed Tariffs on Mexico over Border Security
Section 301 China Tariffs (Tranche 4a Announcement to Implementation)
Proposed Tariffs on European Union over Airbus Subsidies (Escalation threats)
Liberation Day Tariffs / Broad Sweeping Global Tariff Threats (Historical analogous sweeps)

coverage_note: 6 named cases representing major tariff escalation events with explicit advance windows; estimated population universe is roughly 8 to 10 comparable high-stakes escalations.
known_gaps: Excludes minor product-specific exclusions and rapidly shifting daily threat-and-withdrawal cycles that do not reach formal multi-month scheduled implementation dates.
skeleton: Threats issued by the executive branch regarding major regional trade partners featuring explicit deadlines: evaluated across major historical trade disputes where negotiation windows ran alongside implementation threats.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 6 instances equals 66 percent base rate of implementation.
validity_reason: Base rate reflects enduring executive trade policy mechanics under Section 232/301 authorities, remaining stable through typical political cycles.
